close_reason:
Already fixed by bd:JMAP-qz9v.35 close (commit fda4e37 this session). Both concerns the bead raises are resolved:

1. **'type_name: &'static str' locks call sites to string literals**: signature now reads 'type_name: &str' (crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs ~line 412). Parameterised fixtures can pass computed values. The internal storage keys still require &'static str, so the dispatch rebinds the accepted input to the matching literal — mirrors the canonical jmap-calendars-server pattern (bd:JMAP-ic0j.69).

2. **Typo silently corrupts the store**: seed_object now panics with an actionable message naming the typo and the known type-name list ('AddressBook', 'ContactCard') at the seed boundary. Test added: seed_object_rejects_unknown_type_name in mod seed_object_validation_tests.

Verified at HEAD via grep + the new unit tests covering the four panic cases + the non-static-str positive control test seed_object_accepts_non_static_type_name. The bead's PROPAGATION concern (sibling cookie-cutter divergence) is tracked at bd:JMAP-flv7 for tasks-server (the only remaining sibling with seed_object that still has the gap).
description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs:251-266

SIGNATURE:
    pub fn seed_object(
        &self,
        account_id: &str,
        type_name: &'static str,
        id: &str,
        value: serde_json::Value,
    )

USAGE (integration tests, tests/contacts_tests.rs:84-87 etc.):
    backend.seed_object("acc1", "AddressBook", "ab1", address_book_fixture(...));
    backend.seed_object("acc1", "ContactCard", "card1", contact_card_fixture(...));

CALLER CONTRACT PROBLEM:
The `type_name: &'static str` parameter is stringly-typed. Valid values
are "AddressBook" and "ContactCard" (matched by `O::TYPE_NAME` in the
backend). The signature does not communicate which strings are valid;
callers must read the source. A typo like `"Addressbook"` or
`"ContactCardd"` compiles fine, runs without error during seeding, and
silently corrupts the store — `get_objects::<AddressBook>` will fail to
find the seeded fixture, leaving the test author to debug the fixture
plumbing rather than getting a fail-fast at the seed call site.

Once this crate ships seed_object with a `&'static str` parameter, we
cannot promote it to a sealed enum or to `O: JmapObject` type-parameter
form (the obvious cleanups) without breaking every caller. The
&'static str bound makes even runtime-typed callers (rare for test
fixtures, but possible) impossible without leaking the &'static
requirement.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
- That an invalid type_name will produce an error.
- That refactoring "AddressBook" → AddressBook::TYPE_NAME inside the
  test will not silently relocate the seeded data into a new bucket.

RECOMMENDED (any one of):
(a) Generic: `pub fn seed_object<O: JmapObject>(&self, account_id: &Id,
    id: &Id, value: serde_json::Value)`. Caller writes
    `seed_object::<AddressBook>(...)` and the type system enforces.
(b) Sealed enum: `pub enum SeedType { AddressBook, ContactCard }` and
    accept that. New variants are non-breaking via #[non_exhaustive].
(c) Two separate helpers: `seed_address_book` / `seed_contact_card`.

WORKSPACE NOTE:
This helper exists only in contacts-server, not in the canonical
jmap-mail-server. If kept, the canonical-template propagation rule
applies — add to mail-server (and the other 5 extension servers) with
matching shape, or remove from contacts-server.
title: MemoryBackend::seed_object stringly-typed type_name: &'static str — locks call sites to string literals
